Executive Summary
MSEDCL PPA Ph-1 is escalated from STANDARD to P1. The AI model suggested P2, but a business rule (PPA penalty exposure) set the final priority at P1 because realistic first time charging is 405 days after the SCOD of 2026-04-29.

The Rule Engine on planned P6 dates gave P2, and the AI model also gave P2 (priority score 50, confidence 0.995). The business rule raised the final result to P1 because this PPA project will charge after SCOD and carries liquidated damages.

Key Drivers
• Realistic FTC is 2027-06-08, 405 days after the SCOD of 2026-04-29; the deadline is already missed.
• PPA commitment carries a penalty if late, and LD exposure is confirmed.
• The LTA (2026-07-31) came after SCOD, but charging is 312 days after the LTA, so transmission no longer explains the delay.

• Material is not the issue: balance ordering is 0.0 MWp, inventory is 202.4 MWp against 202.5 MWp required, and 159.1 MWp is in transit.

• FTC Risk: The P6 FTC date of 2026-11-29 is optimistic against the realistic FTC of 2027-06-08. Construction pace is the cause, since modules mounted are 0%.

• Transmission Risk: Transmission is not the constraint. The LTA came after the deadline but before realistic charging.

• Hold new ordering, since balance ordering is 0.0 MWp. Keep the 159.1 MWp in transit on track for when the site can take it.

explanation.text:
Executive Summary
MSEDCL PPA Ph-1 is set to P2. Both the AI model and the rule engine predicted P2. The P1 guardrail was reversed on review because the project is fully ordered with adequate inventory and has no planning flags. The projected delay is driven by site readiness, and the PPA exposure keeps it above standard.

Rule vs AI Assessment
The Rule Engine on planned P6 dates gave P2, and the AI model also predicted P2 with 0.995 probability. The PPA penalty guardrail that raised it to P1 was removed because the delay is not supply or transmission related, and client rules say not to artificially increase priority for fully ordered projects with inventory and no flags.

Key Drivers
• Realistic FTC of 2027-05-25 is 391 days after SCOD (2026-04-29); the deadline is already missed.
• PPA commitment with liquidated damages exposure for charging after SCOD.
• Site readiness delay of 177 days; structure is at 0% and modules mounted are at 0%.
• Material is not the constraint: balance ordering is 0.0 MWp, and inventory of 168.6 MWp covers the 168.8 MWp requirement, with 132.6 MWp more in transit.
• Planned FTC (P6) of 2026-11-29 falls after the LTA of 2026-07-31, which itself came after SCOD.

Risks Identified
• FTC Risk: Realistic first time charging is 2027-05-25, well beyond SCOD and later than the P6 FTC of 2026-11-29, unless construction pace improves.
• Vendor Capacity Risk: Not a current constraint: no quota issue, no vendor capacity delay beyond LTA, and supply delay if ordered today is 0 days.
• Transmission Risk: Transmission is no longer the constraint. LTA (2026-07-31) comes before realistic charging, so the delay is not explained by waiting for transmission.

Business Impact
• SCOD impact: SCOD of 2026-04-29 is missed, with charging 391 days after the deadline.
• LTA impact: LTA came after SCOD but before realistic charging, so it does not drive the delay. Site readiness does.
• LD impact: Liquidated damages exposure is confirmed, as a PPA project charging after SCOD carries penalties. Each additional day of delay adds to it.

Recommended Actions
• Treat the project as P2 and review it regularly with project leadership.
• Focus on construction pace: accelerate structure and module mounting, as the binding constraint is site readiness.
• Do not place extra orders or pull shipments forward, since this would only add yard stock; balance ordering is already 0.0 MWp.
• Re-baseline the construction plan against the realistic FTC of 2027-05-25 and identify recovery steps to bring it closer to SCOD.
• Quantify the LD exposure with the commercial team and prepare a mitigation plan.

Executive Summary
No further module ordering is needed for MSEDCL PPA Ph-1, as all 168.8 MWp requirement is already covered by 301.0 MWp ordered. The AI projects charging on 2027-05-25, 391 days after the SCOD of 2026-04-29, driven by site readiness rather than supply.

Rule vs AI Assessment
The Rule Engine shows an ordering date of 2026-07-09 and TC of 2026-10-15 (FTC 2026-11-29), while the AI shows nothing left to order and TC of 2027-04-10. The gap comes from site progress (177 days of delay), not procurement; the rule engine's 98-day lead time compares with a measured 30 days (P90 97) for ALMM supply.

Key Drivers
• Nothing left to order: Balance Ordering is 0.0 MWp.
• Inventory of 168.6 MWp already covers 100% of capacity, with 132.6 MWp more in transit.
• Site readiness is the binding constraint: structure and modules mounted are at 0%.
• Material delay is 0 days and transmission delay is 0 days; progress accounts for the full 177-day shift.
• AI confidence is low (0.21), so the projected dates carry considerable uncertainty.

Risks Identified
• FTC Risk: HIGH. Projected first time charging on 2027-05-25 is 391 days after the SCOD deadline; site readiness sets the date.
• Vendor Capacity Risk: Low. No vendor quota move and no vendor capacity delay beyond LTA; nothing remains to order.
• Transmission Risk: Not a constraint. LTA (2026-07-31) came after the deadline but before realistic charging.

Business Impact
• SCOD impact: SCOD of 2026-04-29 is missed, with charging projected 391 days later.
• LTA impact: LTA of 2026-07-31 falls before projected charging, so transmission is no longer the constraint.
• LD impact: Liquidated damages exposure is YES, as this PPA project is charging after SCOD.

Recommended Actions
• Escalate to the project head to speed up structure work (steel supply, crews), since site readiness sets the charging date.
• Pace deliveries to structure readiness, as earlier delivery only adds yard stock.
• Track shipment milestones weekly against the predicted delivery date.
• Review the P6 piles figure (8130%) and the construction progress data for accuracy.
• Prepare for liquidated damages exposure on this PPA project.

Executive Summary

Rule vs AI Assessment

Executive Summary
The AI sets ASEJ6PL_S07_FT_300MW_PPA at P1, an upgrade from its current STANDARD. The realistic first time charging (FTC) date of 2027-06-04 is 125 days after the SCOD of 2027-01-30, and as a PPA project it carries liquidated damages (LD) exposure.

Rule vs AI Assessment
The Rule Engine (on planned P6 dates) and the AI both give P1, and no business rule overrode the result; the AI model set the final priority. The AI score of 99.8 with 0.997 confidence supports the Rule Engine view.

Key Drivers
• Realistic FTC of 2027-06-04 falls 125 days after the SCOD of 2027-01-30
• PPA commitment: charging after SCOD carries liquidated damages
• Site readiness delay of 145 days; structures are not ready (modules mounted 0%)
• Planner shortfall against the FTC date is 122 days (P6 FTC 2027-01-10)
• Module inventory, receipts and transit are all 0 MWp against a 405 MWp requirement, though balance ordering is 0 MWp

Risks Identified
• FTC Risk: FTC is at risk: the planned P6 FTC of 2027-01-10 is not achievable, and realistic charging slips to 2027-06-04.
• Vendor Capacity Risk: No vendor constraint is binding: the monthly quota is not full, there is no vendor delay beyond LTA, and the supply delay if ordered today is 0 days.
• Transmission Risk: Low. Transmission is ready by the deadline (LTA 2026-12-31), and FTC is not after LTA.

Business Impact
• SCOD impact: The SCOD of 2027-01-30 is missed by 125 days if the current construction pace continues.
• LTA impact: No LTA impact. LTA is not the binding constraint.
• LD impact: Liquidated damages are likely, since this PPA project would charge after SCOD.

Recommended Actions
• Escalate the project to P1 and give it management attention.
• Focus on construction pace, since site readiness is the binding constraint and ordering or shipping earlier only adds yard stock.
• Prepare a recovery plan to close the 145-day site readiness delay, starting with structures and module mounting.
• Review the P6 construction progress data (piles 2940%, structure 140%) for accuracy.
• Track progress weekly against the FTC and SCOD dates, and assess LD exposure.

explanation.text:
Executive Summary
MSEDCL PPA Ph-1 is set at P1, an escalation from its current STANDARD priority. The PPA penalty business rule set this result over the AI model's P2, because realistic first time charging (2027-07-17) is 444 days after SCOD (2026-04-29).

Rule vs AI Assessment
The Rule Engine on planned P6 dates gave P2, and the AI model also predicted P2 (confidence 0.995, score 50). The final P1 was set by the business rule for PPA penalty exposure, not by the model. Charging comes 167 days after the LTA (2027-01-31), so waiting for transmission no longer explains the delay.

Key Drivers
• SCOD (2026-04-29) is already missed, with realistic FTC 444 days after it.
• PPA commitment carries liquidated damages for late charging.
• Full balance of 135 MWp is still to be ordered, with zero inventory, receipts and transit.
• Site readiness is the binding constraint: structures are at 0% and the site readiness delay is 168 days.
• FTC is at risk, with a planner shortfall of 92 days.

Risks Identified
• FTC Risk: Planned FTC (P6) is 2027-01-30, but the realistic FTC is 2027-07-17, with a 92-day planner shortfall.
• Vendor Capacity Risk: No vendor quota or capacity delay is flagged. Supply delay if ordered today is 74 days, so ordering is not the main constraint.
• Transmission Risk: Transmission is not the constraint. The LTA (2027-01-31) falls before realistic charging.

Business Impact
• SCOD impact: The SCOD deadline is missed, with charging expected 444 days after 2026-04-29.
• LTA impact: The LTA came after SCOD but before realistic charging, so it does not explain the delay.
• LD impact: LD exposure is confirmed: a PPA project charging after SCOD carries liquidated damages, and this grows with every further day of delay.

Recommended Actions
• Treat the project as P1 and escalate it to senior management review.
• Focus on construction pace, especially structure erection, since site readiness is the binding constraint.
• Place the 135 MWp balance order in line with the site schedule, so material does not simply sit as yard stock.
• Quantify LD exposure and prepare a recovery plan against the 2026-04-29 SCOD.
• Track construction progress and ordering weekly against the realistic FTC date of 2027-07-17.

explanation.text:
Executive Summary
The AI sets MSEDCL PPA Ph-3 at P1, an upgrade from the current STANDARD priority, with a score of 99.5 and confidence of 0.994. The project is a PPA with the full 151.9 MWp still to order, no inventory at site, and a vendor quota that is already full.

Rule vs AI Assessment
The Rule Engine, working from planned P6 dates, gives P2 because ordering is overdue. The AI result is P1, one level higher. No business rule overrode it, so the AI model set the final priority.

Key Drivers
• PPA commitment carries a penalty if the project is late.
• The full balance of 151.9 MWp (100% of capacity) is still to be ordered.
• Inventory at site is 0.0 MWp, with no receipts and nothing in transit.
• The vendor monthly quota is full, so the order was moved, and vendor capacity delay extends beyond LTA.
• The planner shows FTC at risk by 61 days, and the P6 FTC date is 2027-02-14.

Risks Identified
• FTC Risk: The planner flags FTC at risk by 61 days. The realistic FTC is 2027-04-19, against a P6 FTC date of 2027-02-14. The margin before the SCOD deadline is thin.
• Vendor Capacity Risk: The vendor monthly quota is full and the order has been moved. Vendor capacity delay extends beyond LTA, and supply would take 21 days if ordered today.
• Transmission Risk: No transmission risk now. LTA (2026-12-31) is ready by the deadline and does not bind the project.

Business Impact
• SCOD impact: SCOD (2027-04-29) is currently met with 10 days of margin. Without priority, further slippage in ordering or site work could use up this margin.
• LTA impact: LTA is ready by the deadline, so there is no impact now.
• LD impact: No LD exposure while SCOD is met. As a PPA project, any delay beyond SCOD would carry a penalty.

Recommended Actions
• Upgrade the project to P1 and increase procurement attention.
• Place the 151.9 MWp order now and secure vendor allocation despite the full monthly quota.
• Focus on construction pace, since site readiness is the binding constraint (structures not ready, 64 days of site readiness delay) and earlier shipping would only add yard stock.
• Align material delivery with site readiness so modules arrive when structures are ready.
• Track ordering, vendor allocation and the 10-day SCOD margin weekly.

ai_review_changes.before:
Executive Summary
AI sets MLP T1 (PPA) to P1, an upgrade from the current STANDARD priority. The realistic first time charging date of 2028-01-14 falls 350 days after the AOP deadline of 2027-01-29, so liquidated damages exposure is likely.

Rule vs AI Assessment
The Rule Engine (on planned P6 dates) and the AI both give P1, so they agree. No business rule override was applied; the AI model set the final priority.

Key Drivers
• Realistic FTC is 350 days after the AOP deadline (2027-01-29); the deadline status is MISSED.
• PPA commitment carries liquidated damages if charging is late.
• Balance ordering of 496.9 MWp remains, 71% of capacity.
• Module inventory at site is only 10.1 MWp, with nothing in transit.
• Site readiness delay is 273 days, and structures are not ready.

Risks Identified
• FTC Risk: Realistic FTC of 2028-01-14 is well beyond the P6 planned FTC of 2027-04-16 and the AOP deadline.
• Vendor Capacity Risk: No vendor quota or capacity delay is flagged currently; supply delay if ordered today is 0 days.
• Transmission Risk: No LTA date is available, so transmission readiness cannot be confirmed. Transmission is not the binding constraint.

Business Impact
• SCOD impact: No SCOD date is provided. Charging is predicted 350 days after the AOP deadline, so the commitment will be missed without intervention.
• LTA impact: LTA is missing, so its impact cannot be assessed. It is not currently the constraint.
• LD impact: LD exposure is YES. A PPA project charging after its deadline carries liquidated damages.

Recommended Actions
• Treat the project as P1 and escalate site construction pace (piles, structures, module mounting) as the main lever, since site readiness is the binding constraint.
• Set a recovery plan targeting the 273-day site readiness delay, with weekly tracking.
• Time the remaining 496.9 MWp of ordering to site readiness, so ordering earlier does not just add yard stock.
• Confirm the LTA date with the transmission team to close the data gap.
• Quantify the LD exposure and brief management on the 350-day deadline gap.

Executive Summary
AI says to order now (15-Oct-26), essentially in line with the rule date of 17-Oct-26. However, the AI projects first time charging on 14-Jan-28, 350 days after the AOP of 29-Jan-27, and site readiness, not supply, is the cause.

Rule vs AI Assessment
The ordering dates are close (AI 15-Oct-26 vs Rule 17-Oct-26), but the AI expects modules at site on 17-Jan-27 (latest likely 16-Feb-27) versus the rule's 02-Mar-27. This is because measured SEA supplier lead time is 94 days (P90 124) against 136 days in the rule engine. The AI's order-by date of 13-Jun-26 has already passed.

Key Drivers
• Site readiness delay of 273 days sets the charging date; material delay and transmission delay are both 0 days.
• 496.9 MWp is still unordered across the project, with only 10.1 MWp in inventory and nothing in transit.
• Structure work is behind plan by 6 points, and there is an inventory shortage at site.
• Measured supplier lead time is 94 days (P90 124) versus 136 days in the rule engine.
• AI shows 456.1 MWp needed at site in Oct-26 and 40.8 MWp in Nov-26; the rule engine shows Mar-27 and Apr-27.

Risks Identified
• FTC Risk: Projected first time charging is 14-Jan-28, 350 days after the AOP of 29-Jan-27. Risk level is HIGH, and confidence is low (0.18).
• Vendor Capacity Risk: The vendor monthly quota has not moved the order, but the ordering window has passed, so any further delay risks losing the vendor slot.
• Transmission Risk: No LTA date is available, so transmission readiness cannot be assessed.

Business Impact
• SCOD impact: No SCOD date is available. Charging is projected well after the AOP deadline.
• LTA impact: No LTA date is available, so there is no transmission delay in the projection.
• LD impact: Liquidated damages exposure is YES, because this PPA project is projected to charge after the deadline.

Recommended Actions
• Place the order now and secure the vendor slot.
• Escalate to the project head to speed up structure work (steel supply, crews).
• Pace deliveries to structure readiness, because earlier delivery only adds yard stock.
• Track shipment milestones weekly against the predicted TC date of 17-Jan-27.
• Confirm the LTA and SCOD dates to complete the risk assessment.

Executive Summary
AI and the Rule Engine both set this PPA project at P1, an upgrade from the current STANDARD. The realistic first time charging date of 2027-08-28 falls 53 days after the AOP deadline of 2027-07-06, and the project carries LD exposure.

Rule vs AI Assessment
The Rule Engine (on planned P6 dates) and the AI model agree on P1, and no business rule overrode the result. The AI's realistic charging view confirms the deadline miss that the planned dates point to.

Key Drivers
• Realistic FTC of 2027-08-28 is 53 days after the AOP deadline of 2027-07-06.
• PPA commitment: charging after the deadline carries liquidated damages.
• Full balance of 337.5 MWp is still to be ordered (100% of capacity).

• Site readiness is the binding constraint: a 64-day delay, with piles, structure and module mounting all at 0%.

• Transmission Risk: No LTA date is available, so transmission readiness cannot be confirmed. Transmission is not the binding constraint.

Business Impact
• SCOD impact: The deadline is missed by 53 days. No SCOD date is provided, and the deadline used is the AOP of 2027-07-06.
• LTA impact: LTA is not available, so no LTA gap can be assessed. It is not currently binding charging.
• LD impact: LD exposure is YES. As a PPA project charging after the deadline, it carries liquidated damages for the delay.

Recommended Actions
• Treat the project as P1 and escalate management attention on site readiness.
• Accelerate construction pace (piles, structures, module mounting), since this is the binding constraint, not ordering.
• Place the 337.5 MWp order on a schedule that matches the recovered site readiness, to avoid adding yard stock early.
• Obtain and confirm the LTA date so transmission readiness can be assessed.
• Track the recovery plan weekly against the 2027-07-06 deadline and the LD exposure.

ai_review_changes.before:
Executive Summary
The AI confirms P1 for MSEDCL PPA Ph-3, an upgrade from the current STANDARD priority. The realistic first time charging date of 2027-07-29 falls 91 days after the SCOD of 2027-04-29, which exposes this PPA project to liquidated damages.

Rule vs AI Assessment
The Rule Engine on planned P6 dates gives P1, and the AI result is also P1, so the two agree. No business rule override was applied; the AI model set the final priority.

Key Drivers
• Realistic FTC of 2027-07-29 is 91 days after the SCOD deadline of 2027-04-29
• PPA commitment carries a penalty if late
• Balance ordering is 67.5 MWp, 100% of capacity, with no receipts and no transit
• Module inventory at site is 0.0 MWp
• Vendor monthly quota is full, and vendor capacity delay extends beyond LTA

Risks Identified
• FTC Risk: P6 FTC of 2027-03-05 is at risk, with a planner shortfall of 31.0 days. Realistic FTC slips to 2027-07-29. Site readiness delay is 146 days, and piles, structure and module mounting are all at 0%.
• Vendor Capacity Risk: Vendor monthly quota is full, so quota has moved, and vendor capacity delay runs beyond LTA. Supply delay if ordered today is 2 days.
• Transmission Risk: Not a binding constraint. Transmission is ready by the deadline (LTA 2027-03-31), and LTA does not bind.

Business Impact
• SCOD impact: SCOD is missed, with charging 91 days after 2027-04-29.
• LTA impact: No LTA impact. Transmission is ready by the deadline, so the delay comes from site readiness and not from the grid.
• LD impact: Liquidated damages exposure is YES, because a PPA project charging after SCOD carries LDs.

Recommended Actions
• Treat the project as P1 and escalate it in the planning and review forums.
• Focus first on construction pace (piles, structures, module mounting), since site readiness is the binding constraint and earlier shipping only adds yard stock.
• Place the 67.5 MWp balance order and secure vendor allocation now, given the full monthly quota.
• Sequence deliveries to match structure readiness so that modules do not sit idle in the yard.
• Track construction progress, ordering and LD exposure weekly against the SCOD of 2027-04-29.
Liquidated damages exposure is YES, because this PPA project is projected to charge after SCOD.

Rule vs AI Assessment
The Rule Engine expects modules at site on 2027-01-19 (98-day lead time), while the AI result shows 2027-05-01 (latest likely 2027-06-14). The gap comes mainly from slow site progress, not procurement: measured supplier lead time is 52 days (96 at the longest) against the 98 assumed by the rule engine.

Key Drivers
• Site readiness is the binding constraint: piles, structure and modules mounted are all at 0%, pushing charging 146 days past the P6 date.
• All 67.5 MWp is still unordered, with no inventory, receipts or modules in transit.
• Vendor monthly quota was full, so the planner's order was moved.
• Measured ALMM lead time of 52 days (96 at the longest) is shorter than the rule engine's 98 days.
• LTA of 2027-03-31 is not a constraint; transmission is ready by the deadline.

Risks Identified
• FTC Risk: Projected first time charging is 2027-07-29, 91 days after the SCOD of 2027-04-29. The planner shortfall is 31 days. Confidence in this forecast is low (0.21).
• Vendor Capacity Risk: Vendor quota is full and a vendor capacity delay beyond LTA is flagged, so ordering later than 2027-03-10 could push delivery out further.

Business Impact
• SCOD impact: SCOD of 2027-04-29 is missed by 91 days.
• LTA impact: No impact. LTA of 2027-03-31 is not later than the deadline, and transmission is ready by the deadline.
• LD impact: Liquidated damages exposure is YES, because this PPA project is projected to charge after SCOD.

Recommended Actions
• Place the order by 2027-03-10 and secure the vendor slot.
• Escalate to the project head to speed up structure work (steel supply, crews), since site readiness sets the charging date.
• Pace deliveries to structure readiness, as earlier delivery only adds yard stock.
• Track shipment milestones weekly against the predicted delivery date.

ai_review_changes.before:
Executive Summary
AI recommends ordering the remaining 15.7 MWp by 2027-06-04, about 352 days later than the Rule Engine date of 2026-06-17. Charging is projected for 2028-03-31, 429 days after the AOP of 2027-01-27, because the LTA falls after the deadline.

Rule vs AI Assessment
The Rule Engine orders by 2026-06-17 with modules at site by 2026-10-31, while AI places the order on 2027-06-04 with delivery on 2027-07-01 (latest likely 2027-09-05). The gap comes from transmission: the LTA of 2028-03-31 lets the phase wait, and measured China lead time is 27 days (P90 93) against 136 days in the rule engine. Confidence is low at 0.2.

Key Drivers
• Only 15.7 MWp remains to order out of 816 MWp, and the modules are needed at site in Sep-27.
• Inventory of 391.3 MWp and receipts of 800.3 MWp already cover current erection, with nothing in transit.
• Transmission delay of 472 days (LTA after the deadline) is the binding constraint; site progress and material delays contribute 0 days.
• Measured supplier lead time of 27 days (P90 93) is much shorter than the 136 days assumed by the Rule Engine.
• Vendor quota did not move the order, so quota is not a factor.

Risks Identified
• FTC Risk: HIGH risk: projected charging on 2028-03-31 is 429 days after the AOP of 2027-01-27, so the deadline is missed. The P6 FTC date of 2026-12-15 is not achievable.
• Transmission Risk: The LTA of 2028-03-31 is after the deadline, so transmission, not module supply, limits export.

Business Impact
• SCOD impact: Charging after the deadline is projected. The SCOD date is not available in the project data.
• LTA impact: The LTA of 2028-03-31 is the binding constraint and extends the phase to the LTA date.
• LD impact: Liquidated damages exposure: YES. A PPA project charging after SCOD carries liquidated damages.

Recommended Actions
• Place the order for the remaining 15.7 MWp by 2027-06-04 and secure the vendor slot.
• Escalate the transmission (LTA) date, as it is the main cause of the delay.
• Pace deliveries to structure readiness, since earlier delivery only adds yard stock.
• Track shipment milestones weekly against the predicted delivery date of 2027-07-01.
• Review the liquidated damages exposure with the commercial team.
